summary: The shared control-transaction fence, ported from WorkStore._control_task / _control_record: receipt replay, revision fencing, and the checkpoint-event receipt record. All functions are pub(crate) and run on the caller's open Tx.
responsibilities: control_task: SELECT * FROM forge_agent.coding_tasks WHERE owner_id=$1 AND project_alias=$2 AND id=$3 FOR UPDATE; no row -> rejected(404, not_found). Then SELECT action,intent_digest,receipt_json FROM forge_agent.coding_control_receipts WHERE owner_id=$1 AND project_alias=$2 AND task_id=$3 AND idempotency_key=$4; when a receipt exists: action or intent mismatch -> rejected(409, idempotency_conflict), else return it as replay. Then revision != expected_revision -> rejected(409, revision_conflict); status not in {awaiting_review, completed} -> rejected(409, not_reviewable). Returns the task row plus the optional replay receipt.

control_record: adds actor to the receipt object; UPDATE forge_agent.coding_tasks SET revision=$1, updated_at=clock_timestamp() WHERE owner_id=$2 AND project_alias=$3 AND id=$4 AND revision=$5 with $1 = expected+1 and $5 = expected; when the rowcount is not 1, re-read the revision and tolerate it only when it already equals expected+1 (a same-task repair may have advanced it), else rejected(409, revision_conflict). Then INSERT INTO forge_agent.coding_control_receipts(owner_id,project_alias,task_id,action,idempotency_key,intent_digest,base_revision,result_revision,receipt_json) VALUES($1..$8); then insert_event kind checkpoint with the receipt as payload; then notify.
invariants: control_task's status gate is exactly Python's: {awaiting_review, completed}; callers add their own mode/status checks after it.
The task row is returned whole (SELECT *) because callers read many columns by name.
control_record's emitted event kind is checkpoint and its payload is the receipt including the actor.
